title: Safe tools for minidsh
brief: Build minidsh's tool system on the plugin kernel, in src/tools.ts and a few small plugins. A 'tools' registry service holds every tool and gives the model only schemas. Each call is parsed and validated against its schema. Every call goes through one fixed pipeline: log tool/call, tools/pre-execute, validate, tools/execute, tools/post-execute, log tool/result. On top of the pipeline add a y/n prompt for risky tools where only an exact y proceeds, a batch runner that runs concurrency-safe calls together while keeping results in order, a post-execute listener that saves oversized results to a file, and an edit tool that replaces one exact match, only after a read, with a version check and an atomic write. Every failure must reach the model as a tool error result paired with its call id.

starter.note: ToolRegistry, parseArgs, checkArgs, runToolCall and runBatch.
askPerson(question, policy, signal) returning 'allowed-once' | 'rejected' | 'cancelled' | 'unavailable', and the approvals plugin.
The outputSpill plugin, a tools/post-execute listener writing to .minidsh/spill/<call id>.txt.
read_file and edit tools sharing a map of path to version.
Checks run with npx tsx that feed hand-written ToolCall objects through runBatch with a fake session.

hints: Keep runToolCall's last line, the tool/result append, reachable from every path: deny, unknown tool, bad JSON, bad arguments, thrown error.
Never let a hook change call.arguments. If a plugin wants different behaviour, it denies or replaces the result.
Treat isConcurrencySafe as safe only when it returns exactly true; a missing method or undefined means the call runs alone.
Write each batch result into results[index], so finishing order cannot change the order the model sees.
For spill, test with a 50,000-character string: with keep 2000 the note should say 46000 characters omitted.
In the edit tool, use text.replace(old, () => replacement) so a dollar sign in the new text is not treated as a pattern.
Test approval with the policy set to never first; it should reject without touching the terminal.

rubric.criterion: Tools register into a 'tools' service with disposers, and only name, description and parameters reach the request
Empty arguments become {}, broken JSON and schema mismatches become specific error results, and the tool never runs on bad input
Every call follows the fixed sequence with pre, execute and post waterfall hooks, logged at both ends, and hooks cannot rewrite arguments
Risky calls ask the person; only an exact y proceeds, once, and no terminal or a never policy means denial
Consecutive concurrency-safe calls run together up to a limit, unsafe calls act as barriers, and results keep the model's order
Results over the limit are saved to a file named by call id and replaced by head, tail, path and a hint
Edits require a prior read and an unchanged version, refuse zero or ambiguous matches, keep line endings and write through a temp file and rename

milestones.title: Registry and validation
milestones.body: Provide the ToolRegistry as a 'tools' service and register read_file and current_time from plugins. Feed in a call to an unknown tool, a call with broken JSON and a call missing a required field; each must return a specific Error: result with the right toolCallId, and none may run the tool.

milestones.title: The pipeline and a timeout
milestones.body: Write runToolCall with the six fixed steps and move the agent loop to call it. Add a timeout plugin on tools/execute and a tool that sleeps 2 seconds; with ms set to 500 the result must be the timeout error, and the session must hold both tool/call and tool/result events.

milestones.title: Asking the person
milestones.body: Add askPerson and the approvals plugin with run_command marked risky. Run minidsh in a terminal and ask it to delete a folder: answer n and check the model explains instead of retrying another way. Then run it with stdin piped from a file and check the call is denied as unavailable.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx src/main.ts "delete the build folder"

milestones.title: Batches and spill
milestones.body: Write runBatch and the outputSpill plugin. A batch of read, read, edit, read must run the first two together and the last after the edit, with results in the original order. A command printing 50,000 characters must come back as head, note and tail, with the full text saved under .minidsh/spill.

milestones.title: The safe edit tool
milestones.body: Write read_file and edit sharing a version map. Check that an edit before reading is refused, an ambiguous edit is refused with the match count, a file changed after reading is refused as stale, and a successful edit keeps CRLF line endings. Then ask minidsh to change a port number in a real file.
milestones.checkCmd: npx tsx src/main.ts "change the port in config.ts from 3000 to 8080"
